newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka's silica attracts foreign firms.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka's silica attracts foreign firms.

text.p: Five foreign companies are negotiating with Sri Lanka's Geological Survey and Mines Bureau to set up facilities to mine and process the island's high-grade silica quartz, a government official said on Thursday.

"Sri Lankan silica quartz has a very high purity -- about 99.5 percent," a Mines Bureau official said. "Because of the high grade or purity of our silica quartz we want to keep the resource as much as possible and promote some industry."
The foreign firms were from Japan, Sweden, Germany and the United States, the official said, declining to identify the companies.
Silica is used in the manufacture of semiconductors, electronic circuitry, optical fibres, ceramics, glass, pigments and pharmaceuticals, he said.
"It is capital-intensive to manufacture products while the initial processing is also energy-intensive," he added.
Some 7,300 tonnes of quartz were exported last year, up from 4,600 tonnes in 1995, most of it to Japan, the official said.
The Geological Survey and Mines Bureau is now processing 23 applications for exploration licenses and has so far granted eight mining licenses, the Bureau official also said.
"Our policy is not to allow mineral resources to be exported in raw form," he said. "We want to encourage the export of value-added products."
The government plans to encourage the setting up of value-added mineral industries under a proposed new draft mineral industries policy, he said.
